verdict.reasoning: Patient reports anxiety and poor sleep: 'I've been feeling really anxious over the past few months… it's really impacting on like on the rest of my life, like my sleep' and 'maybe three, four hours I'm getting now.' Palpitations: 'I find my heart kind of racing' and 'I really thought my heart was racing so much, I thought I was going to have a heart attack.' Duration about two months: 'I think I would say maybe about two months or so. I've been feeling like this.'

Onset and job change: 'I think I would say maybe about two months or so. I've been feeling like this and that's probably coincides with me starting a new job… which I would say it's quite stressful.' New, retail head-office job: 'I work for a fashion retailer in the head office team and it's just a brand new sector. I've never worked in retail before.'
Patient describes dread of work and boss: 'I just really dread going there. I just hate speaking to her, I hate seeing everyone and really worried about whether I'm doing well or not.'

Daily/morning anxiety and difficulty getting out of bed: 'I just get really nervous every morning about leaving the house' and 'I don't want to go to work in the morning so I just find no way I can't get out of bed.'

Sleep-onset insomnia and short sleep: 'I can't get to sleep for hours and hours and hours… Not for ages. I'm lying awake all night' and 'maybe three, four hours I'm getting now.' Waking before alarm with racing heart and panic: 'I do have an alarm, but I find myself waking up before that because I'm just. My heart is racing.'

Irregular palpitations lasting minutes to ~10 minutes and new: 'Does it feel like a regular fast beat or an irregular beat?' Patient: 'Irregular, I think.' Duration: 'a couple of minutes… the other day I was actually just sort of lying there for, like, holding my hand on my chest for, like, 10 minutes.' New in last couple of months: 'this is only in the past sort of like, couple of months as I say that I've been experiencing this.'

Denies true chest pain but notes discomfort with fast heart: 'Any chest pain with that?' Patient: 'No. Well, yeah, it's painful when the heart. When my heart is being fat, but yeah.' This reflects no distinct chest pain but discomfort linked to rapid heartbeat.

Low energy, anhedonia, on edge, socializing less, reduced running/tennis: 'It's just really, really low. I'm finding now that I'm just. I find no enjoyment at all… anything that previously was really fun is just not enjoyable. And I'm like, yeah, on edge the whole time.' Socializing: 'I avoid them in so much that I feel like I'm… I know that I'm not going to have fun because I don't want to go out and do things that I would normally have done.' Hobbies/exercise: 'I did used to like to go running and to play tennis and stuff, but now… I'm just not going out to do that quite so much.'

Public transport stressful and anxiety mainly work-focused: 'I find public transport really stressful in a way, especially being on the tube because it's quite getting warmer, so it's just really airless.' Also: 'the majority of it, because my life is just so focused around work right now, the majority of it is focused around work as well.'
No previous similar episodes: 'Before this, did you have Any similar times in your life when you felt like this?' Patient: 'Not really, no… I've never felt anything that's bad before.'

Low mood, no suicidal ideation, good support: 'I'm pretty much down. Like, I don't enjoy being with my day at all… constant feeling of just being a bit down, a bit unhappy.' Suicidal ideation: 'I haven't had any suicidal thoughts or any thoughts that have been that extreme.' Support: 'I have a good support system. Like, I do have a good family and stuff.'

Eating regular, no major appetite change, more chocolate: 'Probably not. Significant changes, maybe? No, I wouldn't say that. I wouldn't say I'm eating, like, much differently.' 'Oh. I probably have more chocolate than normal just because I feel so down.' And 'You're eating regularly otherwise?' Patient: 'Yeah.'

No prior therapy, open to one-to-one: 'I haven't sought any other.' And when asked, 'would you be happy to have some one to one therapy?' Patient: 'Yeah, yeah, I think so. I've never done that before, but yeah.'
Maternal history of depression: 'I talked to my mum because she also suffers from, or she's suffered from like depression in the past.'
Living situation: 'Who do you live with at home?' Patient: 'Yeah, I live with my parents. With my parents.'
Alcohol pattern: 'probably quite a lot on the Friday or Saturday day… I probably go over my limit just on those days anyway. And then like maybe a glass of wine during the week.'
Occasional smoker: 'Do you smoke or take any other drugs or anything?' Patient: 'I try not to smoke, but I do occasionally.'

Denies other drugs: same exchange: 'Do you smoke or take any other drugs or anything?' Patient: 'I try not to smoke, but I do occasionally, but I don't take them.' (context indicating no other drugs).
Workplace: 'So I work for a fashion retailer in the head office team.'

Work-related anxiety with insomnia, functional impact, no SI: Content throughout describes anxiety linked to work and boss, poor sleep, reduced enjoyment and activities. SI explicitly denied: 'I haven't had any suicidal thoughts.' Clinician summarizes this in plan focusing on anxiety and sleep: 'Some people with anxiety, they do need to take medication… helping with your sleep patterns.'

Clinician view on palpitations: 'In terms of palpitations, it is most likely to be associated with anxiety.' Brief morning episodes perceived irregular and without true chest pain are described earlier: irregular ('Irregular, I think'), lasting a few to 10 minutes, and patient denies clear chest pain ('Any chest pain with that?' 'No. Well, yeah, it's painful when…').
Self-referral to talking therapies/CBT: 'you can self refer via the NHS for what we call like talking therapy, which is a type of behavioral therapy… So I can send you the link for that.'

Online resources to start now: 'In the meantime… There are some online resources that are really helpful. Put the details on there and you can get on with them straight away and try and work through them as well.'
Sleep hygiene advice: 'I'll put some more information on your notes about helping with your sleep patterns and things like that.'

Safety-netting: 'if you're feeling like it's not helping at all or your anxiety is getting worse to the point where you can't cope with work or you can't just do your normal things day to day, then it's important for you to give us a call back and just discuss that further.'
Medication considered but not first-line: 'some people with anxiety, they do need to take medication to control that, but that's not something that we suggest in the first instance.'
Blood tests and patient to call: 'it's probably worth having a couple of basic blood tests… So if you call this line, you can arrange the. Have the blood test done.'
Follow-up timing: 'arranging a GP follow up a week after you've had the test so we can just go through the results with you.'
Clinician observation of distress: 'what about your mood day to day? I mean, I can see that you're quite distressed by it…' explicitly notes the patient appears quite distressed.
